radiusSource: Radius 0.0618 Jupiter radii from the NASA Exoplanet Archive's calculated radius (its Chen & Kipping 2017 mass-radius relationship): a model, not a measurement, since Proxima Centauri d does not transit (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/pscp_calc.html): 4,418.2 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.000818 +/- 0.00012 Jupiter masses (Suárez Mascareño et al. (2025), A&A, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202553728, Table 3: minimum mass (m sin i) 0.26 +/- 0.038 Earth masses from the star's radial velocities; the same table gives 0.357 +/- 0.072 Earth masses for an orbit in the star's equatorial plane, tilted 47 degrees, https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202553728) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.
orbitalPeriodSource: Suárez Mascareño et al. (2025), A&A, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202553728, Table 3, a fit of the star's radial velocities with the eccentricity fixed to zero (a/R* is its 0.02881 au over the star's recorded 98,094 km); the orbit's plane is assumed, from the star's rotation axis in Klein et al. (2021, MNRAS 500, 1844) (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202553728): P 5.12338 d

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius in the shared neutral gray. No image, color, map or oblateness of Proxima Centauri d is measured; only its size, mass and orbit are.

massSource: 0.000818 Jupiter masses: Suárez Mascareño et al. (2025), A&A, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202553728, Table 3: minimum mass (m sin i) 0.26 +/- 0.038 Earth masses from the star's radial velocities; the same table gives 0.357 +/- 0.072 Earth masses for an orbit in the star's equatorial plane, tilted 47 degrees (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202553728).
